auditor_value: As served (launch 90° above horizontal): vertical launch, x = 0 throughout, projectile returns to O at t = 4√2 ≈ 5.66 s and never reaches a point P on the incline. For the 45° launch in the figure: (a) t = 7 s, (b) OP = 175 m (x = 140 m, drop 105 m).

findings.note: The question as served says the launch is directed 90° above the horizontal; the solution uses 45° (steps[0]: cos45°, sin45°) without stating that it is departing from the served text. At 90° the launch is vertical, x(t) = 0 for all t, the projectile returns to O at t = 2u/g = 4√2 ≈ 5.66 s and never meets the incline at a point P away from O, so 7 s and 175 m do not answer the problem printed. The answer is correct only for the 45° launch shown in the figure.
findings.fix: Either the question text must read 45° (matching the figure), or the solution must open by stating that the figure shows 45° and that the printed 90° is inconsistent with a landing point P on the slope, and then solve for 45°.

findings.note: Uses a launch angle of 45° that the served question does not give; the served text gives 90°, for which uₓ = 0 and u_y = 20√2 m/s.

findings.quote: taking the incline's direction as positive x
findings.note: x is the horizontal axis (x(t) = 20t uses the horizontal component), not the direction along the incline; a reader can take this to mean x runs along the slope.
findings.fix: taking the horizontal direction toward the lower end of the incline as positive x

question_defect: Question text gives the launch direction as 90° above the horizontal while the figure_description gives 45°; the two conflict, and with 90° there is no landing point P on the slope, so the served text is internally inconsistent. The solution solves the 45° version without saying so.
notes: All other lines are correct for the 45° problem: 20t − 5t² = −15t gives t = 7 s, x = 140 m, OP = 140/0.8 = 175 m. The common_mistakes entry (t = 1 s, OP = 25 m for an upward incline) checks out numerically.
